detailed_description: The AI Prompt Template Generator builds reusable, parameterized prompt templates featuring variable placeholders (e.g., {{variable}}), clear behavioral constraints, output format definitions, sample variable values, and a review checklist. Running completely in your browser without external server calls or AI API tokens, it standardizes prompt libraries for team workflows, AI agents, and content pipelines.
usage_steps: Enter the core task description using double-curly braces for variables (e.g., 'Summarize {{notes}} for {{audience}}')
List the variable names to extract and generate structured placeholders
Specify desired tone, output format specifications, and operational constraints
Toggle example values to preview populated prompt instances alongside the raw template
Review the variable documentation table and copy the reusable template or sample prompt
usage_examples: Create a customer support response template with {{issue}}, {{user_tier}}, and {{resolution}} variables
Build a weekly sprint report prompt template with {{completed_tasks}}, {{blockers}}, and {{next_steps}}
Standardize a blog post generator template with {{topic}}, {{target_audience}}, and {{keywords}}
Generate code documentation prompt templates with {{function_signature}} and {{edge_cases}}

faqs.question: How are variables defined in the prompt template?
faqs.answer: Variables use the standard double-curly brace syntax like {{variable_name}}, which is automatically recognized and indexed into a dedicated variable table.

faqs.question: Is the prompt template generation done locally?
faqs.answer: Yes. All template formatting, variable parsing, and checklist generation run deterministically in your browser without making server requests or consuming LLM API credits.

faqs.question: Can I preview how the template looks with actual data?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can enable the 'Include example values' option to view both the parameterized template and a populated concrete prompt example.
